\chapter{Complexity — Circuit Eval}

\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Complexity.CircuitComplexity.CircuitEval}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Accepting circuit encodings]
\lean{BoolCircuit.CVAL}
\label{BoolCircuit.CVAL}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.IsFaninTwo, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.encode, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.eval, Turing.pairEncode}
The language consists of exactly those Boolean strings that encode a pair of a Boolean
input list $x$ and a directed acyclic circuit $C$ with one input for each entry of $x$,
such that every gate of $C$ has fan-in at most two and evaluating $C$ on $x$ yields
true.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Accepting circuit encodings with prefixes]
\lean{BoolCircuit.CVALPrefix}
\label{BoolCircuit.CVALPrefix}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.IsFaninTwo, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.encode, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.eval, Turing.pairEncode}
The language consists of exactly those Boolean strings that encode a pair of a Boolean
list $x$ and a directed acyclic circuit $C$ with $n$ inputs, where every gate has fan-in
at most two, $n$ is at most the length of $x$, and evaluating $C$ on the first $n$
entries of $x$—using false for any missing entry—yields true.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Circuit-value validation]
\lean{BoolCircuit.mem_CVAL_iff}
\label{BoolCircuit.mem_CVAL_iff}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.CVAL, BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.verdict, BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.verdict_pairEncode, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.encode, Turing.eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode, Turing.pairDecode}
\difficulty{5}
For every bit string $z$, membership in the circuit-value language is equivalent to the
specified circuit-code evaluator returning true on $z$. The language consists of pair
encodings of a circuit code and an input string such that the code describes a
well-formed circuit with fan-in at most two, the input length equals the circuit's
number of input variables, and the circuit accepts that input.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Prefix circuit validation]
\lean{BoolCircuit.mem_CVALPrefix_iff}
\label{BoolCircuit.mem_CVALPrefix_iff}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.CVALPrefix, BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.verdict, BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.verdict_pairEncode, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.encode, Turing.eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode, Turing.pairDecode}
\difficulty{4}
For every bit string $z$, membership in the prefix circuit-value language is equivalent
to the specified circuit-code evaluator returning true on $z$. The language consists of
pair encodings of a circuit code and an input string for which a well-formed circuit
with fan-in at most two accepts the first $n$ bits of that string, for some $n$ no
greater than its length.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time decision from a verdict characterization]
\lean{BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.decidesInTime_of_verdict}
\label{BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.decidesInTime_of_verdict}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.evalTM, BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.evalTM_computes, BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.verdict, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInTime, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{4}
Let $e$ be a Boolean exactness flag and let $L$ be a language of Boolean words. If a
word $z$ belongs to $L$ exactly when the machine’s verdict on $z$ with flag $e$ is true,
then the circuit-evaluation machine with flag $e$ decides $L$ in time $12(n+1)^2$ on
every input of length $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Circuit evaluator decides circuit value]
\lean{BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.evalTM_decidesInTime_CVAL}
\label{BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.evalTM_decidesInTime_CVAL}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.CVAL, BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.decidesInTime_of_verdict, BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.evalTM, BoolCircuit.mem_CVAL_iff, Turing.FinTM.DecidesInTime}
\difficulty{1}
The machine in exact mode decides the language of encodings of fan-in-two Boolean
circuits together with inputs on which they evaluate to true. On every Boolean input
word $x$, it halts within $12(|x|+1)^2$ steps and outputs the one-bit indicator of
whether $x$ belongs to that language.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time decidability of circuit evaluation]
\lean{BoolCircuit.CVAL_mem_P}
\label{BoolCircuit.CVAL_mem_P}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.CVAL, BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.evalTM_decidesInTime_CVAL, Complexity.P, Complexity.mem_P_iff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $L$ consist of the bit strings that encode a pair $(C,x)$ by doubling every bit of
the circuit encoding $C$, appending the separator $01$, and then appending $x$, where
$C$ is a directed acyclic Boolean circuit with $|x|$ input vertices, each gate has
fan-in at most two, and $C$ evaluates to true on $x$. Then $L$ is decidable in
polynomial time by a finite-state multitape Turing machine.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time decidability of prefix circuit evaluation]
\lean{BoolCircuit.CVALPrefix_mem_P}
\label{BoolCircuit.CVALPrefix_mem_P}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.CVALPrefix, BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.decidesInTime_of_verdict, BoolCircuit.mem_CVALPrefix_iff, Complexity.P, Complexity.mem_P_iff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $L$ consist of the bit strings that encode a pair $(C,x)$ by doubling every bit of
the circuit encoding $C$, appending the separator $01$, and then appending $x$, where
$C$ is a directed acyclic Boolean circuit with $n$ input vertices, each gate has fan-in
at most two, $n\leq |x|$, and $C$ evaluates to true on the first $n$ bits of $x$. Then
$L$ is decidable in polynomial time by a finite-state multitape Turing machine.
\end{theorem}
